trust_decision.summary: Whether a sealed OAuth check cookie (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) may be honoured for the provider currently handling a callback is decided in parseCookie, and the provider identity must be written into the sealed payload by sealCookie when the cookie is minted; at the pinned commit neither side records or compares the provider, and the cookie names are the same for every provider, so a cookie minted for provider A is accepted on provider B's callback.

landing_point.why: parseCookie is the single place where every check cookie's value is trusted, and it only tests that a value exists; state.use, pkce.use and nonce.use (checks.ts:125, 173, 205) all funnel through it, and the cookie names it reads are provider-agnostic (utils/cookie.ts:102-120).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about OAuth state/nonce/PKCE check cookies, and getToken() is a separate session-token helper for middleware and API routes that never sees an OAuth check cookie, so it can be argued outside the described fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The redirect-proxy hop: the origin app stores its callback URL as `origin` in the inner state JWT (state.create(options, data)), and the proxy decodes that state and redirects the browser to the origin BEFORE any check cookie is read or validated - the proxy cannot hold the origin's cookie. A fix that requires a provider-bound check cookie at the proxy hop, or that binds the inner state JWT to a provider, breaks the documented redirectProxyUrl flow.

legacy sealed cookie that has no provider field (minted before the fix) - must be rejected, not treated as matching
getToken({raw: true}) and getToken({raw: false}) over that malformed header

O8b_injection_room.sibling: webauthnChallenge - a fourth sealed check cookie in the same CookiesOptions map, created and consumed through the same sealCookie/parseCookie pair but never mentioned by the advisory
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the obvious copy-paste of the state/nonce/pkce pattern in the same file; a maintainer adding passkey support would clone sealCookie/parseCookie and could omit the provider field, and a solver who only patches the three OAuth `use()` helpers leaves it open while a fix in the shared helpers covers it for free.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new per-provider check minted at sign-in (a second `response_mode`/prompt/origin cookie) cloned from the state/pkce/nonce trio
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the only minting site, so any new provider-bound artifact is added here; nothing in the file's shape forces the author to record provider.id.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new consumer that reads a check cookie inline instead of going through checks.*.use, bypassing parseCookie entirely
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleOAuth already reaches for the three checks individually; a refactor or a new check (e.g. a code-exchange binding) would naturally be written next to those calls.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: provider binding on the inner state JWT (state.decode) used by the redirect proxy, mirroring the cookie binding
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same author extending the same fix would plausibly reach for the state payload next; doing so is exactly the over-broad change that breaks the proxy, which makes it a realistic sibling to plant.
